slot.brief: Give a Fischer projection of a two-chiral-centre molecule in the figure; ask students to rank/identify the correct R/S assignment and enantiomer/diastereomer relation among drawn structures.

stem: For the three Fischer projections of 2,3-dibromopentane shown, which option correctly gives their configurations and the relationships of I–II and I–III?
options: I: $(2R,3S)$; II: $(2S,3S)$; III: $(2S,3R)$; I–II are enantiomers and I–III are diastereomers.
I: $(2R,3S)$; II: $(2S,3S)$; III: $(2S,3R)$; I–II are diastereomers and I–III are enantiomers.
I: $(2S,3R)$; II: $(2R,3R)$; III: $(2R,3S)$; I–II are diastereomers and I–III are identical.
I: $(2R,3R)$; II: $(2S,3R)$; III: $(2S,3S)$; I–II are identical and I–III are enantiomers.

verdicts.working: 2,3-Dibromopentane has two distinct stereocenters (CH3 vs C2H5 ends), so no meso form: inverting both centers gives enantiomers, inverting one gives diastereomers. Checking each option's stated relationships against its own configurations: (A) (2R,3S)/(2S,3S) differ at one center → diastereomers ✓; (2R,3S)/(2S,3R) differ at both → enantiomers ✓. B, C, D all misstate these relationships (B swaps them; C calls enantiomers identical; D calls diastereomers identical). Only A is internally consistent, so it must be the intended answer even though the figure fails to show projections I–III.
issues: Figure defect: the question refers to three Fischer projections labeled I, II, III, but the image shows only a single bond-line (zig-zag) structure of 2,3-dibromopentane with no labels or Fischer projections; the stated configurations cannot be verified from the figure. The answer is recoverable only because option A is the sole internally consistent choice.

working:
At C2: $\text{Br}>\text{C3 chain}>\text{CH}_3>\text{H}$; at C3: $\text{Br}>\text{C2 chain}>\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3>\text{H}$. Horizontal $\text{H}$ is toward the viewer: I is $(2R,3S)$, II is $(2S,3S)$, III is $(2S,3R)$. I–II differ at one centre; I–III invert both.

Independent check: 2,3-Dibromopentane has two distinct stereocenters (CH3 vs C2H5 ends), so no meso form: inverting both centers gives enantiomers, inverting one gives diastereomers. Checking each option's stated relationships against its own configurations: (A) (2R,3S)/(2S,3S) differ at one center → diastereomers ✓; (2R,3S)/(2S,3R) differ at both → enantiomers ✓. B, C, D all misstate these relationships (B swaps them; C calls enantiomers identical; D calls diastereomers identical). Only A is internally consistent, so it must be the intended answer even though the figure fails to show projections I–III.
solution: At C2, priorities are $\text{Br}>\text{C3 chain}>\text{CH}_3>\text{H}$; at C3, they are $\text{Br}>\text{C2 chain}>\text{C}_2\text{H}_5>\text{H}$. Accounting for horizontal groups pointing toward the viewer gives I $(2R,3S)$, II $(2S,3S)$, and III $(2S,3R)$. I and II differ at one stereocentre, so they are diastereomers; I and III differ at both, so they are enantiomers. (B)

figure.description: Draw three Fischer projections side by side, labelled I, II and III, each for 2,3-dibromopentane. In each, the vertical chain has CH3 at the top, the C2 intersection above the C3 intersection, and CH2CH3 at the bottom; vertical bonds point away from the viewer and horizontal bonds point toward the viewer. Projection I: at both C2 and C3, Br is on the left and H on the right. Projection II: at C2, H is on the left and Br on the right; at C3, Br is on the left and H on the right. Projection III: at both C2 and C3, H is on the left and Br on the right.
